transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Maplewood CISO), Marcus Hale (Maplewood Head of Cloud), Sophie Kim (Maplewood Security Engineer)

Auto-summary: quick SOC2 / ISO posture review, agreed next steps to share reports and mapping, schedule follow-up for Dedicated network diagram.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, really appreciate the time. This is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya from our security engineering team. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Lena: Doing well, thanks. We'll keep this focused — we've got a checklist to run through for SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
[00:20] Jordan: Perfect. The goal is just to make sure our controls and your compliance needs line up, show where things live in our Trust Center, and call out any gaps for Dedicated or Private deployments.
[00:28] Priya: Hi everyone, hi. I'll take the technical bits — RBAC, SSO, audit logs, KMS, and the control mappings part.
[00:35] Marcus: Quick practical question up front: if we moved to Dedicated, do audit logs live in our VPC or are they forwarded to your console? We need to understand custody.
[00:45] Priya: Good question. For Hosted API audit logs are retained in Redwood's logging infra and we provide exports. For Dedicated and Private we can route logs to your syslog/s3 endpoint in your VPC. There was a note in the docs that the export can be pushed to your S3 bucket with encryption in transit.
[00:58] Sophie: When you say "export" — is that raw request/response payloads or metadata level? We have PHI concerns so we need to limit full payload retention.
[01:08] Priya: By default it's metadata and headers, timestamps, tokens consumed, latencies. Full payloads are opt-in and can be disabled. For customers with PHI we usually recommend disabling full payload capture and using event-level logs plus hashes for traceability. There's a config flag on Dedicated.
[01:22] Speaker 1: so um... just to chime, the KV cash —
[01:25] Priya: KV cache, yes. The transcript sometimes says cash, we mean cache. The KV cache is in-memory on the serving nodes and not persisted by default.
[01:33] Marcus: Ok that helps. Next on SOC 2: scope — does Redwood's SOC 2 Type II cover Dedicated and Private controls or only hosted?
[01:42] Jordan: Our SOC 2 Type II covers Redwood's hosted platform services and the control environment for the control plane. For Dedicated we have a delineation: the control matrix maps which controls apply to customer-managed infra vs Redwood-managed. We'll share a mapping spreadsheet that explains which controls remain Redwood responsibility and which are in-scope for customer operations.
[02:00] Lena: And ISO 27001? We need to confirm the certification scope and whether it covers the dev and production environment.
[02:07] Jordan: ISO 27001 certificate covers Redwood's core platform and operational processes. It's included in the Trust Center. Priya can show where the certificate and the scope doc sit.
[02:16] Priya: Right — I have a quick screen shot link in the notes but I won't screenshare here. The Trust Center has the ISO cert, SOC 2 report redacted, control mappings, and our pen test summary. Access is by invite; we can grant Maplewood read-only access to the Trust Center for your security and audit teams.
[02:33] Sophie: Will the SOC 2 report be redacted? We typically need the full report for our vendor risk team, but we understand some sections might be redacted for other customers.
[02:42] Jordan: The standard distribution is a redacted SOC 2 Type II for contractual review. For customers with a signed NDA we can provide a less-redacted or full report depending on the legal terms. We'll work with your procurement team on that.
[02:55] Marcus: Good. On SSO: we use Okta with SCIM group provisioning and strict RBAC. How does Redwood handle role mapping?
[03:05] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Roles are mapped on our side to RBAC groups; you can sync groups from Okta and map to the pre-defined Redwood roles or a custom role set. We also support just-in-time provisioning if you prefer.
[03:18] Sophie: Audit trail for admin actions — do you have an immutable admin audit log? We need to show who changed RBAC roles and when.
[03:27] Priya: Yes, admin actions are in the audit log with actor identity via SSO, timestamp, and action. For Dedicated deployments, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. For Hosted, we retain admin action logs for 365 days by default; retention can be extended via an add-on.
[03:43] Lena: Is there tamper-resistance — like append-only or signatures?
[03:47] Priya: We maintain append-only logs in our logging backend with immutability controls and can sign exports if needed. For high-assurance customers we recommend forwarding to your own secure storage for eventual immutability requirements.
[03:58] Jordan: One more note on encryption: data in transit is TLS 1.2+ and at-rest uses AES-256. For customer-managed keys we support KMS integration — either AWS KMS or a bring-your-own HSM model for Private deployments.
[04:12] Marcus: We require CMEK for keys in our Dedicated environment. Is that supported?
[04:16] Priya: Yes, for Dedicated and Private deployments we support CMEK via your KMS. We can provide integration docs; some HSM-backed workflows require a bit of setup but it's supported.
[04:27] Sophie: Is there key rotation automation?
[04:29] Priya: We support automated rotation policies through the KMS, and Redwood's services will fetch the key metadata; we do not store key material ourselves when CMEK is enabled.
[04:37] Speaker 2: um there's also the question of data residency, right?
[04:40] Lena: Yes — we must keep all PHI data in-region (US-East). Does Redwood permit regional isolation for Dedicated?
[04:47] Jordan: Yes. Dedicated pools can be provisioned in a specific region. For Private we can do on-prem or a region-limited deployment. We'll capture region details in the controls mapping spreadsheet.
[04:58] Marcus: Regarding pen tests — do you share the full report or just a summary? Our third-party risk team asks for remediation timelines.
[05:06] Priya: We share a pen test summary in the Trust Center. For deep reviews and remediation timelines we can share more under an NDA. The summary includes issue severity, remediation status, and the dates of fixes.
[05:18] Sophie: On the controls mapping spreadsheet, can you map to our internal control IDs? We use a custom matrix (Maplewood-CTRL-###).
[05:26] Jordan: We can provide a CSV mapping; if you provide your control IDs we can do a crosswalk and return a mapping file. That's part of the deliverables.
[05:35] Lena: Okay. A couple of tricky requirements: e-Discovery — we need the ability to export logs for legal hold. How do you handle that?
[05:44] Priya: Export APIs exist for logs and transcripts. For Hosted we provide export endpoints and S3 export. For Dedicated you can retain logs in your S3 or syslog endpoint and run legal hold on your side. We also support point-in-time exports upon request.
[05:58] Marcus: About retention — what's default retention for embeddings and stored vectors? We plan to use embeddings for search and might need to TTL them after 90 days.
[06:08] Priya: Embeddings stored via Redwood's managed DB have configurable TTLs. For PHI data we recommend storing vectors in your own VPC-managed store. We'll include guidance in the notes.
[06:19] Sophie: One notation: in documentation you mention "Trust Center access" — what's the process and who gets invited?
[06:25] Jordan: We typically invite the CISO or security point person as read-only. Additional users can be added. Invite is via email and uses SSO to sign in. The Trust Center contains the SOC report, ISO cert, pen test summary, and controls mapping artifacts.
[06:39] Lena: Great. Can you also provide sample audit log schema so I can vet it against our SIEM parsers?
[06:45] Priya: Yes, we'll attach a sample JSON schema and a sample export in the shared folder.
[06:53] Jordan: Quick recap — action items: I'll share SOC 2 and ISO cert (NDA if needed), Priya will prepare controls mapping CSV and sample audit log export, Sophie will send region and data residency specifics. We'll set a follow-up week of 4/27 to go over Dedicated network diagram and onboarding steps.
[07:10] Lena: Sounds good. Any other vendors in consideration? We have a note that they looked at BigCloudAI and ModelServeCo.
[07:18] Jordan: Understood — we'll highlight where Redwood differs on dedicated telemetry and control mapping in the follow-up.
[07:24] Sophie: One final small question — do you have an SLA for log delivery/availability? We need 99.9% on telemetry for audit purposes.
[07:33] Priya: Our platform SLA for Dedicated includes 99.9% availability for control plane APIs and telemetry exports; we'll include the exact SLA language in the doc. For Hosted we have tiered SLAs.
[07:45] Marcus: Thanks everybody, we'll review the artifacts when you send them.
[07:48] Jordan: Thank you all — we'll get the report and mapping over by Thursday.
[07:52] Lena: Thanks, bye.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts: "KV cash" = KV cache, speaker labels sometimes generic. References: Trust Center link (to be provided), controls-mapping.csv (to be shared), sample-audit-logs.json (to be shared).

End of transcript.
